To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the responses of the hand to heating and to cold were reduced by repeated immersions in water of these temperatures and that the diminution of responses to both heating and cooling was brought about by the same central nervous process.
the pain, the blood pressure, the heart rate and the sweating responses to the same hand were all reduced by the repeated immersion of that hand in hot water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of repeated heating and cooling of a hand on the sensations and on the cardiovascular responses.
the following questions: (1) Can a person habituate to a painful stimulus, i.e. can he learn to become less responsive to the stimulus?
the effects of habituation on the responses of the human body to heating and cooling, and with the question of whether habituation can be induced by repeated heating or cooling of a part of the body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results show that habituation to heating of a hand can be produced by repeated immersions in warm water, that it is a reversible process which is not caused by any local change in the hand, that it is not accompanied by any change in the sensation of heat, that it is brought about by a central nervous mechanism which is not the same as the mechanism which brings about the conditioned reflex, and that it is not a process of learning or conditioning.

habituation is an acquired decrease in the response to a repeated stimulus, which may occur even when the stimulus is not associated with any other stimulus, and which is not due to fatigue, to a change in the stimulus or to any change in the organ of sense.
habituation is an adaptation to a constant stimulus, which is based on a decrease in responsiveness, and which is not necessarily a conscious process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the responses to heating are modified by habituation but that those to cooling are not.
habituation of responses is not caused by any change in the stimulated part but by a central process.
habituation is not a conditioned reflex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be careful in how we define and measure our metrics.
the more we can understand about the brain, the more likely we are to be able to treat brain disorders.
the brain’s response to stress is not fixed but can be altered.
